Resolves #21868

A board can show the total value in each stage beside its count or WIP limit. Configure `columnSummary: {field: 'amount', formatter: formatCurrency}` once. The column uses its full filtered population, so moving a deal or editing its amount offscreen updates the header. Scrolling the card window skips the sum. The [Board guide](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/c12892413b/learn/guides/datahandling/Board.md#column-summaries) shows the config with a custom deal model.

Evidence: L3 (real Store and Board tests, Chromium pointer drag and rendered headers) → L3 required.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/board/Column.spec.mjs` checks the plain count, WIP and existing controls, finite numeric contributions and zero on an empty column. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same spec changes an offscreen deal, moves it between lanes in the same write as an amount change, filters the store, replaces and detaches it, and enables and removes a custom formatter. |
| AC-3 | Outside-CI: in Chromium on the basic board, enabling the summary for the numeric progress field showed Ready at 0 and In progress at 283. Physically dragging the card worth 86 changed those headers to 86 and 197. The App worker reported the card in Ready. |

## Deltas from ticket

The real-browser drag uses the existing sprint board's numeric progress field. The unit fixture and guide use deal amounts. Clio confirmed the separate sales pipeline example under #21346.

## Test Evidence

The unconfigured board rendered zero summary labels. The drag ran in both Neo Dark and Neo Light at 1440 × 900. Frame critique: the header keeps the numeric total, count and collapse control readable on the same line in both themes. The optional formatter supplies the unit an application needs.

The diff implements the ledger row as written, in the two owners it names, with a scroll-only path that skips the sum. Nothing needs a return cycle; three notes below are follow-up or polish.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Thank you, Emmy. Two choices make this right rather than merely working: the total comes from `Column#windowRecords`, the full filtered population `selectWindow` keeps before it slices, so a virtualized column counts cards it never rendered; and `reconcileColumn(…, {windowOnly: true})` keeps scrolling from paying for a sum whose membership did not change.

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #21868 (Problem, Architectural Reality, Contract Ledger, ACs); `dev`'s `src/board/Column.mjs` (`selectWindow` assigns `windowRecords = records` and returns `records.slice(...)` when sliced; `updateHeader` mutates `header.vdom.cn[0..3]`), and `src/board/Container.mjs` (`reconcileColumn` reads `getColumnRecords(status, lane)`; `onStoreRecordChange` only reconciles on status, order or lane changes).
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** A reactive `columnSummary_` on the board; the sum taken over the column's whole filtered membership inside reconciliation, never over rendered cards; a field-only change of the summed field refreshing just the owning column, even when its card is off-window; the formatter's result rendered as text, not HTML. It must not hardcode a unit or currency, and tests should use a real Store and Board.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `syncSummary()` sums `Number.isFinite` values of `windowRecords`, renders `String(formatter(total))` through `node.text`, and re-renders the header only when the text changed; `onStoreRecordChange` gains the field-only branch; `afterSetStore(null)` and `afterSetColumnSummary` resync; the guide documents the config with a custom model.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with the Body's projection model: the store stays the truth and the header is one more projection of it, so a second view on the same store would show the same total.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: three non-blocking points. (1) Reading order: the summary node is pushed after the toggle and lock, and CSS `order` moves it beside the title, so a screen reader hears "Ready, 11, Collapse column, 86" while the eye reads "Ready 86 11". Inserting it as `cn[1]` would make DOM and visual order agree, at the cost of the fixed indexes `updateHeader` uses today. (2) Every edit of the summed field walks the column's whole population (`O(n)` per change); right for today's boards, worth an incremental sum if a big-data board turns it on. (3) Without a formatter the raw float shows (`0.1 + 0.2` reads `0.30000000000000004`), as the ledger asks; a guide line suggesting a formatter for currency amounts would spare readers that surprise.
